title: Teacher guide: Is it still worth continuing? (Story 1)
intro: This guide supports Story 1 of Tulevaisuuden tähdet with compulsory-education-age students (about 16–20) in adult basic education. The game is a tool for discussion, not a test. A student does not get a star for a right answer: a star arises when a character begins to see a new possibility for themselves.

ul: Study is not clicking, absences have accumulated, and the students would like to move to vocational school but their skills are not yet enough and they have no basic education certificate.

Five situations: in the break room, a task that will not open, who takes someone along, a returned exam and slow progress in studies. They can be done in any order and limited in Settings or with a link ?only=j1,j2.
The dialogue is short everyday Finnish. In situations 4 and 5 the characters are young students with an immigrant background.

Eight stars: I went to class; I do not stay alone but tell an adult about my situation; I found a way to get started; I made room for another; I found a new way to try; and three stars from situation 5 (homework together, helping at home, going out with friends).

A star comes from a choice made but not from a single right one: for example “I found a new way to try” opens when Sami seeks help and agrees a new way to practise. It does not require the next exam to be passed.
A star is never lost. Situations can be revisited to try another path.
Play it yourself. One situation takes about 10 minutes.
The player may invent a name for the character on the start screen. The name is not saved. Use an invented name.
Fill in the support persons’ contact details (responsible teacher, study counsellor) and display them before playing.
The text follows the manuscript. Option D of situation 4 (complaining to the teacher) and the closing message were written to fill gaps in the manuscript: review them.
5 min: safety rules and introduction. 30 min: in pairs, 2–3 situations. 15 min: shared reflection.
Stop at a choice and ask “Why this?” before the group clicks.
Situation 1: Who could help when studying does not interest you? How do you tell them?
Situation 2: How can others notice you need help if you say nothing?
Situation 3: How can you ask someone to join so they do not feel like a bother?
Situation 4: To whom can you send a message when you feel bad after an exam? What can the message say?
Situation 5: How does “later” become an agreed moment and a single task?
Situation 1: option A mentions smoking (“röökille”). Use is not shown in the game.
Situation 4: the exam fails and Sami is ashamed. Do not ask students to show their own exams. Nobody has to show an exam to others.
Situation 5: helping at home. Do not ask students to list their own home responsibilities.
If a student tells something worrying, follow your institution’s procedures and offer a one-to-one conversation. In an emergency call 112.
The photos show Keuda premises. Check usage rights before publishing.
Progress is stored in the browser. On a shared device use “Delete saved progress” in Settings.
